Caprifoliaceae.key_door: opposite leaves + inferior ovary, then split woody Lonicera/Symphoricarpos from herbaceous current Valeriana

Viburnaceae.key_door: woody + opposite leaves + broad clusters of small regular flowers + inferior ovary + drupaceous fruit; compound Sambucus vs simple Viburnum

lineage_lesson: Dipsacales begins well with opposite leaves and inferior ovaries, but family recognition requires flower and fruit architecture. Caprifoliaceae is broad and needs two internal project doors; Viburnaceae is visually tighter.
taxonomy_notes: Valerianella radiata is source provenance for accepted Valeriana woodsiana.
Valerianella amarella is source provenance for accepted Valeriana amarella.
Sambucus nigra subsp. canadensis is a synonym of accepted Sambucus canadensis and should not be double-counted.
Sambucus nigra remains a separate accepted Old World species concept.
Viburnum rufidulum remains accepted and native to Texas under current Kew.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Keep source names visible as provenance, but teach current Valeriana concepts.
Do not use opposite leaves alone to distinguish Caprifoliaceae from Viburnaceae.
